title: Coast Douglas-fir: Ancient Coast Douglas-firs You Can Visit
meta_description: The giant conifer of the Pacific coast. Red Creek Fir holds more wood than any Douglas-fir measured, and Big Lonely Doug stands alone in a clearcut.
intro: Coast Douglas-fir is the tall conifer of the Pacific coast, and on Vancouver Island it grows into some of the largest trees in Canada. The Red Creek Fir near Port Renfrew carries 349 cubic metres of trunk, more than any other Douglas-fir measured, on a girth of 13.3 metres and a height of 74 metres, though its forked crown shows it has lost its top at least twice. An hour away stands Big Lonely Doug, 66 metres tall, left as a single fir in a clearcut after a timber cruiser tied ribbon reading Leave Tree around it in 2011. And in Cathedral Grove, the Big Tree is more than nine metres round and about 76 metres tall by the park's own sign, which puts it at over 800 years old. It survived the windstorm of New Year's Day 1997 that brought down hundreds of its neighbours.
